title: Quran Knowledge
description: Little Muslim → Mid. Short questions for children who know the first Quran basics. Covers preservation, revelation in stages, Hira, Laylat al-Qadr, meanings of familiar short surahs and simple Quran lessons about gratitude, kindness, careful speech, checking reports and good choices. Uses familiar home and classroom situations. An adult may read questions aloud or explain unfamiliar words. All questions are Mid level within the Kids audience.
levelMethod: Mid describes the knowledge and understanding needed across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Builds on first Quran basics through simple meanings, connections between familiar ideas and straightforward applications. No specialist tafsir debate, advanced recitation rules or memorization of reference numbers is required. Level is editorial guidance, not calibrated with children's reading or response data. Quiz performance describes learning needs, not a child's faith or worth.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages and hadith text checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original child-friendly educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Contemporary home and classroom scenarios apply the cited principles; they are not events narrated in the cited verses. The distinction between Allah's preservation of the Quran and possible errors in a typed copy is an educational application. Revelation in stages concerns the Quran's delivery to the Prophet; Laylat al-Qadr questions do not specify a disputed calendar date. Seeking Allah's help does not rule out ordinary help from teachers or caregivers. Religious distinction in Al-Kafirun is not presented as permission to mistreat people of another faith. General teachings about life as a test do not assign adult legal accountability to young children. No question asks children to judge another person's faith or worth. This is not independent scholarly approval or a completed review with children.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: What promise about the Quran is taught in Surah Al-Hijr?

options.text: Allah will preserve it
Its message must change every year
People may replace it with their own ideas
It was never revealed by Allah

questions.explanation: Allah promises to preserve the Quran. We treat its words as revelation, not as something to rewrite according to our preferences.

questions.question: How was the Quran revealed to the Prophet ﷺ over time?

options.text: As a single printed schoolbook
In stages
Only through messages from kings
As stories invented by different classmates

questions.explanation: The Quran was revealed in stages. Its revelation to the Prophet ﷺ did not all happen at one moment.

questions.question: In which cave did the Prophet ﷺ receive the first Quranic revelation?

options.text: A cave named by his classmates
A cave under a royal palace
The cave of Hira
An unnamed cave beside a school

questions.explanation: An authentic report describes the first Quranic revelation coming to the Prophet ﷺ in the cave of Hira.

questions.question: Which special night does Surah Al-Qadr connect with the Quran being sent down?

options.text: The night before every school test
Every child's birthday night
The first night of every week
Laylat al-Qadr

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Qadr connects the Quran's being sent down with Laylat al-Qadr. This is a special night, not a date invented by a quiz.

questions.question: What command appears at the opening of Surah Al-Alaq?

options.text: Read in the name of your Lord
Stop learning forever
Boast that nobody can teach you
Hide every useful book

questions.explanation: The opening verses call for reading in the Lord's name. They also mention Allah teaching people what they did not know.

questions.question: In Al-Fatihah, what do we affirm alongside worshipping Allah alone?

options.text: We worship the sun too
We ask Him for help
We have no need of His help
We choose a different god each day

questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah joins worship of Allah alone with seeking His help. This verse teaches devotion and dependence on Him.

questions.question: What does Surah Al-Ikhlas teach about Allah and birth?

options.text: He was born like a human baby
He has children who become gods
He was not born and has no child
He needs parents to care for Him

questions.explanation: Allah does not have parents or children. Surah Al-Ikhlas teaches this clearly, distinguishing Him from His creation.

questions.question: From what evil do we seek Allah's protection in Surah An-Nas?

options.text: The kindness of a helpful teacher
The sound of every friendly greeting
The good advice of our parents
The evil of harmful whispering

questions.explanation: Surah An-Nas teaches seeking Allah's protection from evil whispering. It describes whisperers from among jinn and people.

questions.question: What does Surah Ad-Duha teach about treating an orphan?

options.text: Do not mistreat the child
Make the child feel unwanted
Treat the child as less important
Ignore the child's dignity

questions.explanation: Surah Ad-Duha forbids mistreating an orphan. A child's family situation is never a reason for cruel treatment.

questions.question: Which failure is criticized near the beginning of Surah Al-Maun?

options.text: Helping arrange a meal for someone hungry
Not encouraging food for people in need
Treating an orphan gently
Caring about another person's hunger

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Maun criticizes harsh treatment of orphans and failure to encourage feeding the poor. These verses call our attention to others' needs.

questions.question: Which army is mentioned in Surah Al-Fil?

options.text: An army of imaginary sea monsters
An army named after a classroom game
The Army of the Elephant
An army made of snowmen

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Fil describes how Allah frustrated the plan of the Army of the Elephant. Its strength did not guarantee success.

questions.question: Which two blessings are mentioned near the end of Surah Quraysh?

options.text: The newest toys and the highest scores
Endless praise and an expensive house
Never needing food and never needing help
Food against hunger and safety against fear

questions.explanation: Surah Quraysh reminds its listeners of food and security from Allah. It calls them to worship the Lord who blessed them.

questions.question: What does Surah Al-Kafirun make clear about the Prophet's ﷺ worship?

options.text: He would not worship what the others worshipped
He would change his religion for every visitor
He would worship every idol in turn
He had no faith of his own

questions.explanation: The surah clearly distinguishes the Prophet's ﷺ worship from the worship addressed in it. He did not agree to exchange his faith.

questions.question: What does the ending of Surah An-Nasr teach the Prophet ﷺ to do?

options.text: Boast that Allah's help was unnecessary
Praise Allah and seek His forgiveness
Stop remembering Allah after success
Insult everyone who needs help

questions.explanation: Surah An-Nasr teaches praising Allah and asking His forgiveness. Success is a time for humility and remembrance, not arrogance.

questions.question: What danger does the opening of Surah At-Takathur warn about?

options.text: Learning useful things with others
Being content with a simple gift
Competition for more distracting us from what matters
Sharing something with a friend

questions.explanation: The surah warns about being consumed by competition for more. Possessions should not distract us from remembering Allah and living well.

questions.question: Which behavior does Surah Al-Humazah warn against?

options.text: Speaking respectfully about others
Encouraging a child who is learning
Giving someone sincere praise
Speaking badly of people and putting them down

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Humazah warns against hurtful attacks on people. It also criticizes greedy reliance on wealth.

questions.question: After mentioning Luqman's wisdom, what does the Quran teach?

options.text: Be grateful to Allah
Pretend every blessing came from ourselves alone
Never recognize a good gift
Use learning only to boast

questions.explanation: The Quran connects Luqman's wisdom with gratitude to Allah. Being grateful benefits the grateful person; Allah needs nothing from us.

questions.question: What does the Quran teach about a report brought by an unreliable person?

options.text: Spread it quickly without checking
Check it before acting in a way that harms others
Treat every rumor as proven truth
Punish someone just because a story sounds exciting

questions.explanation: The verse teaches verification to avoid harming people through ignorance. Acting on an unreliable report can lead to regret.

questions.question: What does Surah Al-Mulk teach about the purpose of life and death?

options.text: A contest to own the most toys
A race to become the loudest person
A test concerning who is best in deeds
A reason to ignore every good choice

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Mulk connects life and death with a test of deeds. It also describes Allah as Almighty and All-Forgiving.

questions.question: What does the ending of Surah Yusuf teach about Quran stories?

options.text: They are invented only for amusement
They have no connection to guidance
They should be changed to make them exciting
They contain lessons for thoughtful people

questions.explanation: The Quran's stories carry lessons and guidance. They are not invented entertainment to rewrite however we like.

questions.question: Does Allah's promise to preserve the Quran mean every phone app is free of typing mistakes?

options.text: No, an app can still contain copying mistakes
Yes, every typed quotation must be perfect
Yes, an app can never miss a word
No, because the Quran has no protection from Allah

questions.explanation: Allah's promise concerns preservation of the Quran. It does not mean every app or typed quotation is free of mistakes.

questions.question: What does revelation in stages mean?

options.text: The message came from different human authors
Passages were revealed at different times
Only the first passage was from Allah
The Prophet ﷺ invented the missing parts

questions.explanation: Revelation in stages describes how Allah sent the Quran to the Prophet ﷺ over time. It does not mean the message had different authors.

questions.question: Why is Hira important when learning about Quran revelation?

options.text: The whole Quran was printed there by a king
Every Quran chapter was written there by a traveler
The first Quranic revelation came to the Prophet ﷺ there
The companions invented revelation there after the Prophet ﷺ

questions.explanation: Hira is connected with the beginning of Quranic revelation. We learn about that event from an authentic report.

questions.question: Why is Laylat al-Qadr important when studying the Quran's revelation?

options.text: The Quran was invented during a school celebration
The Quran must be rewritten on that night yearly
The Quran may only be read on that night
The Quran was sent down on that night

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Qadr links that special night with the Quran's being sent down. It does not limit Quran reading to one night.

questions.question: What do the opening verses of Al-Alaq teach about learning?

options.text: Allah teaches people what they did not know
Learning is always a waste of time
People are born knowing every subject
A pen can give knowledge without Allah

questions.explanation: The opening verses mention reading, the pen and Allah's teaching. Knowledge is a blessing, not a reason to deny our need for Him.

questions.question: Which pair of ideas belongs together in Al-Fatihah's fifth verse?

options.text: Worshipping idols and forgetting Allah
Worshipping Allah alone and asking His help
Needing no guidance and knowing everything
Praising ourselves and rejecting all help

questions.explanation: This verse joins worship of Allah alone with seeking His help. Both belong to the message we recite in Al-Fatihah.

questions.question: Can we describe Allah's family as if He were a human with parents and children?

options.text: Yes, His family is like a larger human family
Yes, every powerful being must have parents
No, Allah has neither parents nor children
No, because He has only children but no parents

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas rules out both parenthood and being born for Allah. We should not describe Him as part of a human family.

questions.question: Does Surah An-Nas teach us to follow every suggestion that encourages wrongdoing?

options.text: Yes, every harmful suggestion must be obeyed
Yes, whispering always makes a wrong choice right
No, it teaches that harmful suggestions can never occur
No, it teaches seeking protection from evil whispering

questions.explanation: The surah teaches turning to Allah for protection. An encouragement toward wrongdoing is not something we must follow.

questions.question: Does Surah Ad-Duha allow mistreating an orphan because their family situation is different?

options.text: No, it specifically forbids mistreating the orphan
Yes, only children with wealthy parents deserve kindness
Yes, a different family situation removes dignity
No, but it says the child must earn basic respect

questions.explanation: The surah protects the orphan from mistreatment. Differences in family circumstances do not make a child less deserving of respect.

questions.question: Does Surah Al-Maun treat concern for hungry people as unimportant?

options.text: Yes, hunger is never anyone else's concern
No, it criticizes failing to encourage their feeding
Yes, people in need should always be ignored
No, but only wealthy people's hunger matters

questions.explanation: These verses connect serious moral failure with neglecting people in need. Concern should lead toward suitable help, not indifference.

questions.question: What does the army's failed plan in Surah Al-Fil teach about worldly strength?

options.text: A large army can never fail
Having elephants guarantees every plan succeeds
A powerful army is not beyond Allah's power
Allah cannot stop people who have weapons

questions.explanation: The army's plan failed despite its strength. The surah reminds us that worldly power is not greater than Allah's power.

questions.question: What response to Allah's gifts does Surah Quraysh call for?

options.text: Forget the giver as soon as we feel comfortable
Claim that food and safety never matter
Boast that Allah owes us every comfort
Worship the Lord who provided food and safety

questions.explanation: The surah connects blessings with worship of Allah. Receiving food and safety should remind us of the One who provides them.

questions.question: Does Surah Al-Kafirun teach changing our worship to match every other religion?

options.text: No, it makes the distinction in worship clear
Yes, our religion must change with every conversation
Yes, every idol becomes part of our worship
No, because it says Muslims have no religion

questions.explanation: The surah teaches a clear religious distinction. It does not ask Muslims to trade their worship for another faith's worship.

questions.question: Does success remove our need to praise Allah and seek His forgiveness?

options.text: Yes, success makes remembrance unnecessary
No, An-Nasr teaches both in the setting of victory
Yes, only people who fail should remember Allah
No, but seeking forgiveness is replaced by boasting

questions.explanation: Surah An-Nasr joins victory with praise and seeking forgiveness. Achievement is not a reason to feel independent of Allah.

questions.question: Is owning a toy itself the problem warned about in At-Takathur?

options.text: Yes, every toy is automatically forbidden
Yes, enjoying any possession is always wrong
No, the warning concerns distracting rivalry for more
No, because greed can never distract anyone

questions.explanation: The warning is about being distracted by rivalry for more. It does not mean simply owning or enjoying a toy is wrong.

questions.question: Does making others laugh turn hurtful mockery into good conduct?

options.text: Yes, laughter makes every insult kind
Yes, popular people may mock anyone
No, but it becomes kind if repeated often
No, the warning against putting people down still matters

questions.explanation: Humiliating someone does not become kind because others laugh. The surah warns against speech that attacks people's dignity.

questions.question: Who benefits when a person is grateful, according to the lesson about Luqman?

options.text: The grateful person
Allah, because He needs people to complete Him
Only people who give expensive gifts
Nobody, because gratitude is pointless

questions.explanation: The verse teaches that gratitude benefits the grateful person. Allah is Self-Sufficient, whether people thank Him or not.

questions.question: Why should we check an unreliable report before acting against someone?

options.text: An exciting story is always true
We might harm someone because the report is wrong
Popularity is better evidence than facts
Checking means we must believe every rumor afterward

questions.explanation: Verification helps prevent harm and regret. A report should not become a reason to mistreat someone before the facts are checked.

questions.question: Which description best matches the test mentioned in Surah Al-Mulk?

options.text: Who can boast the loudest about themselves
Who can avoid every helpful action
How well people act, rather than how many possessions they collect
Who can make others feel least important

questions.explanation: The verse speaks of being best in deeds. Possessions and boasting are not what it presents as the purpose of life.

questions.question: Why should we ask what a Quran story teaches us?

options.text: Only the names in the story ever matter
Every story is meant to teach a guessing trick
Understanding is forbidden when reading stories
Its lessons are part of its purpose

questions.explanation: The Quran invites thoughtful learning from its stories. Understanding the lesson matters alongside remembering the events.

questions.question: A copied verse in an app looks different from your trusted Quran text. What is a sensible next step?

options.text: Ask your teacher to help check the copied text
Assume every app must be free of mistakes
Rewrite the Quran to match the app
Add more words according to your preference

questions.explanation: A copying error should be checked against a reliable Quran text. Allah's preservation of revelation does not make every digital copy error-free.

questions.question: A worksheet says all Quran revelation to Muhammad ﷺ happened in one afternoon. What correction fits?

options.text: The Quran was written by his classmates
The Quran was revealed to him in stages
Only kings received its later passages
The rest was invented whenever someone wanted a story

questions.explanation: The Quran describes revelation in stages. Receiving passages over time is different from receiving the whole message in one afternoon.

questions.question: Sara is labeling a picture of the cave of Hira. Which event should her note mention?

options.text: A king printing the complete Quran
A school inventing its own religious book
The beginning of Quranic revelation to the Prophet ﷺ
The companions making up the first revelation

questions.explanation: The authentic report connects Hira with the first Quranic revelation. Sara's note should describe that event accurately.

questions.question: A class makes a card linking Laylat al-Qadr with revelation. Which sentence belongs on it?

options.text: The Quran was invented at a birthday party
No Quran verse mentions this night
Quran learning is forbidden on every other night
The Quran was sent down on Laylat al-Qadr

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Qadr makes this connection. The card should reflect the Quran's teaching, without inventing a rule restricting when we may learn it.

questions.question: After learning Al-Alaq's opening verses, Adam notices how reading helps him learn. Which thought fits their lesson?

options.text: Learning is a gift for which I can thank Allah
Knowing one word means I need no further learning
A pen deserves worship because it teaches me everything
Learning makes me better than everyone in every way

questions.explanation: The verses connect reading and learning with Allah's generosity. Our ability to learn can remind us to be grateful rather than boastful.

questions.question: Aminah wants her dua to match Al-Fatihah's lesson about seeking help. Which request fits?

options.text: Sun, I worship you and need your guidance
Allah, help me do what is good
My pencil, I pray to you for help
I need no help from Allah at all

questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah directs worship and seeking help to Allah. Aminah can turn to Him in a sincere request.

questions.question: A classmate asks whether Allah was born like people. Which answer follows Al-Ikhlas?

options.text: Yes, He was born in a palace
Yes, but only after creating the sun
No, Allah was not born
No, but He has children who become gods

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas teaches that Allah was not born and has no offspring. He is not part of a human family.

questions.question: A friend quietly urges Hasan to cheat. Which response fits An-Nas's lesson about evil whispering?

options.text: Cheat because a whispered suggestion must be right
Assume saying something quietly makes it kind
Follow the suggestion without thinking
Seek Allah's protection and refuse the dishonest suggestion

questions.explanation: The surah teaches seeking protection from evil whispering, including from people. Hasan can turn to Allah and choose not to cheat.

questions.question: Some classmates mock an orphan's family situation. Which action follows Ad-Duha's teaching?

options.text: Refuse to join in and seek a teacher's help
Repeat the mockery more loudly
Tell the child they deserve cruel treatment
Use their family situation to exclude them

questions.explanation: The surah forbids mistreating an orphan. Respect the child and involve a trusted adult when classmates are causing harm.

questions.question: After studying Al-Maun, your class plans help for hungry families. Which choice fits the lesson?

options.text: Make posters mocking the families
Help a teacher organize a suitable food collection
Insist that hunger is never important
Hide all the donated food for yourself

questions.explanation: Encouraging suitable help for hungry people follows the lesson. A teacher can guide the collection and make sure the help is appropriate.

questions.question: A friend says, "The army in Al-Fil was too strong for its plan to fail." What should you explain?

options.text: The surah says its plan could never fail
Elephants make every army stronger than Allah
Allah frustrated its plan despite its strength
The story teaches that Allah has no power over armies

questions.explanation: Surah Al-Fil describes the army's scheme being defeated. Its size and strength did not place it beyond Allah's power.

questions.question: Maryam has a meal in a safe home after learning Surah Quraysh. Which thought fits its lesson?

options.text: Comfort means I no longer need Allah
People who have less are worth less
Every blessing belongs only to my family
Food and safety are blessings from Allah

questions.explanation: The surah reminds us of food and security from Allah. Maryam can recognize those blessings with gratitude and worship.

questions.question: Yusuf is explaining Al-Kafirun in class. Which summary fits?

options.text: The Prophet ﷺ kept his worship distinct from idol worship
The Prophet ﷺ agreed to worship every idol
Muslims must change their religion to match each visitor
The chapter says Muslims have no faith of their own

questions.explanation: The surah clearly distinguishes the Prophet's ﷺ worship from that addressed in it. Yusuf should explain that distinction accurately.

questions.question: After doing well in a learning activity, what response reflects the humility taught in An-Nasr?

options.text: Declare that Allah's help never matters
Praise Allah instead of boasting, and seek His forgiveness
Mock everyone who found the activity difficult
Say that successful people no longer need Allah

questions.explanation: The surah's instruction is given in the setting of victory. Its lesson encourages humble remembrance rather than pride after success.

questions.question: Ali spends all his time comparing toys and neglects important responsibilities. What better choice fits At-Takathur's warning?

options.text: Demand more toys just to defeat his friends
Stop caring about anything except owning more
Enjoy his things without letting rivalry take over
Decide that another child's belongings determine his worth

questions.explanation: Rivalry for more can become distracting. Ali can enjoy what he has while making time for worship, learning and care for others.

questions.question: Friends invite Sara to make fun of a classmate's appearance. Which choice follows Al-Humazah's warning?

options.text: Invent a crueler joke
Spread the joke to another class
Decide that popular children may insult anyone
Do not join in putting the classmate down

questions.explanation: The surah warns against hurtful attacks on people. Sara can refuse to join the mockery and choose respectful speech.

questions.question: After learning the verse about Luqman's gratitude, Zaynab notices a blessing in her day. What response fits?

options.text: Recognize the blessing and thank Allah
Boast that she has never needed Allah
Treat every gift as something Allah owes her
Claim that gratitude never benefits anyone

questions.explanation: Gratitude benefits the grateful person. Zaynab can recognize Allah's gift without acting as though He depends on her thanks.

questions.question: An unverified story accuses a classmate of stealing. What is a careful choice?

options.text: Share it with everyone before checking
Ask a teacher to check without spreading the accusation
Punish the classmate yourself
Add invented details to make it exciting

questions.explanation: Unreliable accusations can cause real harm. A trusted teacher can help check what happened without spreading an unproven claim.

questions.question: After learning that life involves a test of deeds, which daily goal fits the lesson?

options.text: Collect things only to feel superior
Win attention by humiliating others
Try to make good choices in how I act
Avoid every chance to do something useful

questions.explanation: The verse turns attention to good deeds. A child can practice good choices without treating possessions or popularity as a measure of worth.

questions.question: Your class finishes a Quran story. Which question best helps you learn from it?

options.text: How can we add invented events and call them Quran?
Which character should we turn into a cruel joke?
How can we avoid thinking about its meaning?
What truthful lesson can guide our choices?

questions.explanation: The Quran's stories invite reflection and learning. Discuss the real lesson while keeping the revealed account separate from invented additions.
